highlights: An AI-powered application in development, designed to help users tailor resumes and cover letters to job descriptions using verified professional information.
Building a multi-service architecture with a React/TypeScript frontend and a Java/Spring Boot backend, with AI integration planned for a future phase.
Developing the application incrementally, with attention to automated testing, code formatting, and maintainability.

items.title: Production Cell Simulator
items.technologies: Python 3 · JSON · CSV · UUID · datetime · unittest · unittest.mock · Git · GitHub · Visual Studio Code
highlights: A command-line Python simulator of a manufacturing cell.
Simulates detected and missed sensor signals, tracks produced pieces against the target, and stops when production is complete or the missed-signal limit triggers a sensor fault.
Writes timestamped events and a unique run ID to CSV; includes unit tests for signal handling, work-order outcomes, and fault conditions.

items.title: RunnerRPG
items.technologies: C# · Unity · Unity UI · ScriptableObjects · DOTween · Adobe Illustrator · Adobe Photoshop · Inkscape · Android
highlights: A personal Android RPG prototype built with Unity and C#, featuring turn-based battles, character progression, inventory, and equipment upgrades.
Developed mobile screens for character menus, battle information, inventory, equipment, and progression; created original vector artwork for much of the interface.
Organized character, skill, and equipment data with ScriptableObjects and implemented local save and load; tested gameplay on an Android phone.

items.title: ESP8266 Weather Station and Binary Number Challenge
items.technologies: ESP8266 · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · LEDs · Push button · Buzzer · C++ · Arduino · Wi-Fi · I²C · HTTP · NTP · NTPClient · PinButton · Adafruit GFX · Adafruit SSD1306 · Adafruit Unified Sensor · Adafruit BME280 · Arduino IDE · draw.io

media.alt: Wiring schematic for the ESP8266, SSD1306 OLED, and BME280.

highlights: An ESP8266-based connected weather station and binary-number game combining BME280 sensor readings, an OLED display, and a local web interface.
Added network time and a binary-number challenge in which three LEDs display values from 1 to 7; players select the matching decimal number with a button.
Implemented game feedback: correct answers increase the score, while a wrong answer ends the round and activates a buzzer.

items.title: Connected Weather Station with MicroPython Display and Zabbix
items.technologies: 2× ESP8266 · BME280 · SSD1306 OLED · LEDs · Push buttons · Potentiometer · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · Wi-Fi · HTTP · JSON · I²C · mDNS · Zabbix · PinButton · Adafruit Unified Sensor · Adafruit BME280 · SSD1306 driver · Arduino IDE · draw.io

media.alt: Wiring diagram for the two ESP8266 boards, BME280 sensor, SSD1306 OLED, LEDs, buttons, and potentiometer.

highlights: An IoT weather-station prototype connecting two ESP8266 boards over a local network: one collects BME280 readings and controls LEDs, while the other displays the data.
Exposed sensor measurements and LED status through HTTP endpoints, with JSON data used by the display board.
Configured Zabbix to monitor the sensor readings and LED states.

items.title: IoT Sensor Monitoring with MQTT and Zabbix
items.technologies: 2× ESP8266 · ESP32 · BME280 · GY-521/MPU-6050 · SSD1306 OLED · C++ · Arduino · MicroPython · Wi-Fi · MQTT · HTTP · JSON · Mosquitto · Zabbix · Arduino IDE · draw.io

media.alt: Conceptual system architecture showing three microcontrollers (two ESP8266 boards and one ESP32), sensors, Mosquitto, Zabbix, and data flow.

highlights: An IoT monitoring project using three microcontrollers (two ESP8266 boards and one ESP32) to collect and exchange environmental and motion-sensor data.
Published BME280 readings over MQTT using Mosquitto and exposed environmental and motion data through HTTP/JSON endpoints.
Configured Zabbix to monitor environmental measurements and selected motion-sensor values.

items.title: Translation Company Automation
items.technologies: Python 3 · Shell · PyPDF2 · ReportLab · Crontab · Linux (VM) · Git · GitHub
highlights: A Python automation project for a fictional translation company, streamlining recurring document-processing and business tasks on Linux.
Calculated service prices and generated PDFs with date-stamped watermarks and registry pages.
Organized files, tracked daily revenue, and scheduled recurring scripts with Crontab and Shell.
